claim_checks.source: Proposition 3.7(3), Lemma 3.9 and Theorem 3.10, PDF pp. 20-23 and 27
claim_checks.independent_reason: The signed-permutation rational representation is irreducible with scalar commutant. Z^2 and its even-sum index-two lattice have the same rationalization but no integral equivariant isomorphism: a rational scalar carrying one lattice to the other would have square determinant two. Thus integral non-isomorphism does not imply distinct rational character modules. In the actual construction, split versus anisotropic choices at an auxiliary split prime ensure non-isogeny, and the twisting step retains that distinction.
claim_checks.counterevidence_and_impact: The stronger non-isogeny condition restores the product-closure argument in the main construction. The local lattice witness is not an all-hypotheses Shimura counterexample. The weaker standalone formulation remains unresolved.
claim_checks.correction_scope: Preserve Needs Evidence and the explicit non-isogeny repair; do not assign a substantive severity.

claim_checks.source: Lemma 3.9, PDF pp. 24-25; Getz-Hahn author draft of 22 April 2022, Lemmas A.5.1-A.5.2, printed pp. 482-483 / PDF pp. 498-499
claim_checks.independent_reason: Conjugating diag(1,2) by [[1,1/5],[0,1]] gives [[1,1/5],[0,2]], outside GL2(Z5), although the torus is split. Thus unramifiedness alone does not put its compact subgroup in the prescribed hyperspecial model. The actually checked primary draft requires a torus and Borel subgroup scheme of that integral model. The norm valuation with a general uniformizer is (1/e) times the nonnegative sum of character/cocharacter pairings; positivity and compactness recover the infinite-order conclusion.
claim_checks.counterevidence_and_impact: This local integral-position test is not an all-hypotheses Shimura counterexample. The separate unramified-field assertion under the full original assumptions remains unproved in this check. The 2024 published book was not acquired, so its wording is not asserted.
claim_checks.correction_scope: Retain the report's distinction between the repaired infinite-order argument and the unresolved field/integral-position claim.

claim_checks.independent_reason: An open subgroup contains a product of open subgroups, which is sufficient; it need not itself be a product. The unique conjugator equations permit descent after passing to an algebraically closed overfield. These repairs preserve the uses inspected.
